findings.title: Minted phUSD has no in-suite backing or redemption: hook mints ratio% fresh phUSD per dispatch while up to 100% of the backing sUSDS is LP'd (owner-extractable BPT) or donated out as USDC
findings.rootCause: phUSD mint-debt is accrued per-dispatch on the gross dispatched USDS (default 50%), but the corresponding sUSDS is never escrowed 1:1 as redeemable collateral. It is either added single-sided to the sUSDS/phUSD pool (BPT held on the dispatcher, fully extractable by the owner via withdrawBPT) or, when batchDonationSize is set up to 100%, swapped to USDC and transferred entirely to batchMinter. No phUSD redemption function exists anywhere in V2 scope. The mint-debt basis (per-dispatch, gross) and the backing-retention (per-batch, owner-tunable 0-100%) are disjoint and non-deterministic from a minter's perspective.
findings.leakPath: User pays `price` USDS in NFTMinterV2._executeMint; USDS is forwarded to BalancerPoolerV2 and wrapped to sUSDS. The hook accrues mintDebt += amount*ratio/100 and pull() later mints that much NEW phUSD to `recipient`. The backing sUSDS does not stay escrowed: pool() either LPs it (BPT owner-extractable) or, at batchDonationSize=100, ships 100% of it out as USDC to batchMinter. Worst case: 100% of deposit value exfiltrated AND 0.5 phUSD/USDS freshly printed with zero on-chain backing. Net new unbacked phUSD = ratio% * cumulative USDS mint volume.
findings.notes: ECON-001 (no in-suite backing/redemption, LP branch) and ECON-002 (gross-debt basis vs up-to-100% donation) are two manifestations of the same root cause (minted phUSD decoupled from retained backing); ECON-002 is the donation-amplified worst case and ECON-006 (batch-level vs per-dispatch attribution) is the accounting-basis support. Merged into one High. CAVEAT: phUSD's external/global backing system is not defined in this repo and there is no documentation; intent (collateralized issuance vs discretionary seigniorage) cannot be confirmed from source. Owner trust is OOS for malice, but issuance of unbacked supply is a protocol-economics property independent of owner honesty. FLAG FOR HUMAN REVIEW: severity hinges on the OOS external phUSD backing model — confirm intent before submission as High.

findings.title: NFTMigrator.migrate() per-unit mint loop is unbounded over ERC1155 balance: large holders can be permanently unable to migrate (gas-limit DoS)
findings.rootCause: migrate() runs an outer loop over [1, v1.nextIndex()) and an inner loop `for (j=0; j<balance; j++)` that calls v2.mintFor(...) once per NFT unit held, with a require/revert inside the loop. Total external calls scale with the caller's entire aggregate V1 ERC1155 balance. There is no batch mint (_mintBatch), no pagination, and no partial-migration path; a single failing id reverts the whole migration.
findings.leakPath: A holder with a large aggregate V1 balance (ERC1155 tokenIds can legitimately hold high quantities) makes `balance` external calls in one tx. Once cost exceeds the block gas limit the migration cannot complete in a single transaction and there is no pagination/partial path, so the holder's V1->V2 conversion is permanently blocked. Balances are not user-reducible downward without migrating.
findings.notes: Availability/DoS, no direct fund loss. v1.nextIndex() (outer bound) is owner-bounded and small; the unbounded dimension is per-holder `balance`. Distinct from DEDUP-003 (which is the late-registration index-0 brick, a different root cause). Recommend quantity-aware mintFor / ERC1155 _mint(recipient,id,balance,'') or pagination. SAST-002 (state-change-after-external-call in migrate) and SAST-001/003 reentrancy-on-migrate are folded here as the same code site; reentrancy through trusted V1/V2 contracts found non-exploitable.

findings.title: Late V1 dispatcher registration permanently bricks migrate() for affected holders (index-0 mintFor revert; init/registration ordering coupling between independently-owned contracts)
findings.rootCause: setInitialized() validates non-zero indexMapping for all V1 indexes in [1, v1.nextIndex()) only AT INIT TIME, then flips `initialized` permanently (one-way). V1 NFTMinter and NFTMigrator are independently owned; V1.registerDispatcher increases v1.nextIndex() at any later time. migrate() loops over the LIVE v1.nextIndex(), so a late-registered index N+1 is included with indexMapping[N+1]==0, and v2.mintFor(0,...) reverts ('index not registered') after the burn — reverting the whole tx.
findings.leakPath: (1) Owner maps V1 indexes 1..N and calls setInitialized() — passes. (2) V1 owner later registers a new dispatcher -> V1 index N+1 exists and users mint/hold tokenId N+1. (3) Any such user's migrate() loops to i=N+1, burns the balance first, then calls v2.mintFor(indexMapping[N+1]=0) which reverts; the tx (incl. burn) rolls back. Because the loop is shared, one un-mapped late index blocks migration for every user who also holds it. No fund loss (burn rolled back), but migration is unavailable until the migrator owner manually adds the mapping.
findings.notes: Cross-contract ordering coupling, NOT owner-self-harm: the V1 owner who triggers it need not be the migrator owner. Distinct root cause from DEDUP-002. Recommend migrate() skip (continue) indexes whose indexMapping is 0, or re-validate at migrate time.

findings.title: Donation-phase sUSDS->waUSDC swap uses limitRaw=0 with only a pooler-supplied minUSDC floor, exposing the donation leg to sandwich/MEV when minUSDC is loose
findings.rootCause: In unlockCallback the sUSDS->waUSDC swap is EXACT_IN with limitRaw=0 (accepts any output); the only slippage protection is require(usdcReceived >= minUSDC) checked AFTER the waUSDC->USDC unwrap, with minUSDC supplied by the authorized pooler at pool() call time. There is no on-chain TWAP/oracle reference or enforced max-slippage floor relative to a queried quote.
findings.leakPath: pool() is a public-mempool transaction (authorized-pooler EOA). An attacker observing the pending tx can sandwich the swapPool to push the sUSDS->waUSDC price against the donation and capture the difference, bounded below only by minUSDC. If a pooler passes minUSDC=0 or loosely, up to batchDonationSize% of each batch is extractable — value that would otherwise reach batchMinter.
findings.notes: Mitigated by pool() being onlyAuthorizedPooler + nonReentrant + whenNotPaused and the caller-supplied minUSDC/minBPT floors; severity hinges on whether a sane on-chain floor is required vs delegated to a semi-trusted pooler. SAST-006/007 (unchecked ERC4626.deposit / Balancer swap-settle-addLiquidity returns) and SAST-009 (getIdealBPT == 0 strict equality) touch this same pooling code path; SAST-009 was disproven by symbolic check_zeroBranch_dustDoesNotBypass (dust >= 1 wei does not bypass the zero branch) so it is dropped as noise. SAST-006 retained below as DEDUP-009. FLAG: confirm whether pooler is sufficiently trusted to make this QA vs Medium.

findings.title: setRatio off-by-one (ratio can equal MAX_RATIO=50, NatSpec says strictly <50) and (amount*ratio)/100 truncation silently zeroes phUSD debt on dust dispatches
findings.rootCause: setRatio uses `if (newRatio > MAX_RATIO) revert` but the documented invariant is ratio STRICTLY < MAX_RATIO (50). The operator should be `>=`; as written ratio=50 is accepted and DEFAULT_RATIO is already 50, so the spec's own bound is violated. Separately, added=(amount*ratio)/100 truncates: if amount*ratio<100 the debt rounds to 0 and onDispatch early-returns.
findings.leakPath: Spec deviation: downstream reasoners trusting `ratio < 50` are wrong (actual is ratio <= 50). Truncation under-mints phUSD by (amount*ratio mod 100)/100 wei per dispatch (rounds toward backing, harmless direction); only reachable to zero for sub-2-wei dispatches, unreachable for 18-decimal USDS at realistic prices.
findings.notes: QA/spec deviation. setRatio is onlyOwner; no theft path. Symbolically proven (check_setRatio_allows50 PASS, check_onDispatch_debtMatchesRatio PASS: debt==floor(amount*ratio/100), no over-accrual). Economic safety bound (ratio<=50, at most 50% of USDS becomes phUSD debt) holds per fuzz+symbolic. Recommend `newRatio >= MAX_RATIO` or fix the NatSpec.

findings.title: Constructors lack zero-address validation across NFTMigrator, BurnerV2, GatherV2 (and other V2 components)
findings.rootCause: Constructors set critical immutable/state addresses (v1/v2, token_/burnRecorder_, token_) without non-zero checks. Misconfiguration bricks the relevant flow (revert on external call) rather than causing loss.
findings.leakPath: Owner-deployment misconfiguration only; no external attack path. Bundled QA.
findings.notes: Slither's 15 missing-zero-check results were filtered as noise; this consolidates the LOCAL-flagged constructor cases into one QA bundle item. Low value — include in QA report only.

findings.title: NFTMinterV2 mint path has no reentrancy guard; cross-contract reentrancy gated only by each dispatcher's own nonReentrant (latent defense-in-depth gap, not currently exploitable)
findings.rootCause: NFTMinterV2 inherits no ReentrancyGuard. dispatch() is nonReentrant on the DISPATCHER only, so it blocks re-entry into the same dispatcher but not a re-entrant NFTMinterV2.mint targeting a DIFFERENT dispatcher index. Two callback surfaces exist in the mint tx: hook.onDispatch and the ERC1155 onERC1155Received acceptance callback. Separately, nonReentrant is not the first modifier on BalancerPoolerV2.pool / BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook (SAST-011).
findings.leakPath: No exploit found under the current in-suite hook set: in-scope hooks (DefaultDispatchHook, BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook) make no external calls in onDispatch, and a re-entrant mint of another index simply performs another fully-paid mint with its own price growth (no invariant broken). A FUTURE hook/dispatcher making an external call to attacker code during dispatch would expose the unguarded minter to cross-index reentrancy.
findings.notes: Informational / defense-in-depth. Verified non-exploitable today (BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch only forceApprove+ERC4626.deposit; BurnerV2/GatherV2 no untrusted callback before _mint). Recommend adding nonReentrant to NFTMinterV2._executeMint/mintFor. SAST-011 (modifier ordering) folded in as the same defense-in-depth theme.

findings.title: replaceDispatcher silently re-points already-minted NFTs to a new dispatcher/token/metadata with no migration of existing holders
findings.rootCause: replaceDispatcher(index, newDispatcher) overwrites configs[index].dispatcher, tokenIdToDispatcher[index] and dispatcherToIndex while leaving existing ERC1155 balances for tokenId==index untouched. tokenId is the index, not a per-dispatcher identity, so existing holders' claim semantics, backing and metadata change underneath them.
lines: src/V2/NFTMinterV2.sol:177 (mint fetches token from current config.dispatcher)
findings.leakPath: Owner-only action: uri(index) returns the new dispatcher's metadata and future mints pull the new primeToken; if any downstream redemption keys off tokenIdToDispatcher / dispatcher.primeToken(), pre-replace NFTs would be honored against the new token. No V2-in-scope on-chain redemption exists to exploit this directly, so impact is bounded to metadata/identity drift today.
findings.notes: QA/centralization integrity for the replace mechanism. Owner trust OOS for malice, but the silent semantic change to issued tokens is a design-soundness note for any redemption layer. Recommend a new index for a genuinely different dispatcher, or freezing replace to dispatchers sharing the same primeToken.

findings.title: Unchecked return value of IERC4626(sUSDS).deposit in BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch (shares-minted ignored on core dispatch path)
findings.rootCause: The shares-minted return of IERC4626(_sUSDS).deposit(amount, address(this)) is ignored; the wrapped-share amount is assumed implicitly. If the ERC4626 wrapper mints fewer shares than expected (rounding/fees/partial deposit), downstream donation/pooling accounting can diverge from the actual sUSDS held.
findings.leakPath: Pooling later reads balanceOf(address(this)) rather than the deposit return, so in practice it operates on actual held sUSDS; impact is bounded unless deposit can partial-fill without reverting. Flagged because it is on the core USDS->sUSDS dispatch path.
findings.notes: High-confidence static finding but low real impact since pool() re-reads balanceOf. Kept separate from DEDUP-004 (slippage) as a distinct accounting-hygiene item. Consider QA bundle. SAST-007 (unchecked Balancer swap/settle/addLiquidity returns) folded into DEDUP-004 context.

findings.title: abi.encodePacked with potentially dynamic types feeding keccak256 in NFTMinterV2
findings.rootCause: abi.encodePacked() used with possibly dynamic-length arguments whose packed bytes are hashed; if two distinct argument tuples pack to the same byte string, hash collisions could break uniqueness/identity assumptions (mint keys / dispatcher identifiers).
findings.leakPath: Exploitability depends on whether any hashed argument is dynamic AND attacker-influenced. Needs manual confirmation of what is hashed; if dynamic types are present, switch to abi.encode.
findings.notes: Unverified static lead; could be QA or no-impact. FLAG FOR HUMAN REVIEW: confirm the encoded arguments at line 263 are not dynamic/attacker-controlled before discarding or escalating. V1 mirror (SAST-005, NFTMinter.sol:218) dropped as V1/context scope.

findings.title: Privileged setMinter / single-step Ownable changes lack events or two-step safety (governance monitorability + transfer footgun)
findings.rootCause: ATokenDispatcherV2.setMinter reassigns the privileged minter with no event (reduced off-chain monitorability of a security-critical role change), and all owner-gated V2 contracts use single-step Ownable rather than Ownable2Step (irrecoverable accidental transfer).
findings.leakPath: No external attack; centralization/operational-hygiene. Owner trust is a documented known issue.
findings.notes: QA bundle. setMinter event (SAST-012) and Ownable2Step (SAST-013) merged as the same governance-hygiene theme.
